name: Rice Bread
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: teacupfuls rice-flour wet to a thin paste with cold milk, and boiled four minutes
ingredients.originalText: three teacupfuls rice-flour wet to a thin paste with cold milk, and boiled four minutes

instructions.text: Make a sponge with warm water, yeast, white sugar, lard, and wheat flour
Beat well together and when it has risen (about five hours), add three pints of warm milk and three teacupfuls rice-flour wet to a thin paste with cold milk and boiled four minutes
Stir into the batter when it should be a little more than blood-warm
If not thick enough to make out into dough, add a little wheat-flour
Knead thoroughly and treat as you would wheat bread in the matter of the two risings and baking

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Make a sponge with warm water, yeast, white sugar, lard, and wheat flour
2. Beat well together and when it has risen (about five hours), add three pints of warm milk and three teacupfuls rice-flour wet to a thin paste with cold milk and boiled four minutes
3. Stir into the batter when it should be a little more than blood-warm
4. If not thick enough to make out into dough, add a little wheat-flour
5. Knead thoroughly and treat as you would wheat bread in the matter of the two risings and baking
